title: Monkey Face Emoji 🐵 Meaning and When It Offends
description: The 🐵 monkey face emoji means playful, cheeky fun, but it has also been used as racist abuse. Learn its friendly uses, the risks, and similar monkey emojis.
summary: The 🐵 monkey face emoji is a brown cartoon monkey that most people use for silliness: goofing around, “monkey business,” a cheeky child. It needs care, though. Directed at Black people it is a recognized form of racist abuse, and platforms and sports bodies treat it as such.
meaning: In its ordinary sense, 🐵 is about mischief. Parents call a climbing toddler “my little monkey,” friends use it when they are acting ridiculous, and it fits any message about bananas, zoos, jungle trips or the monkey bars. It has a simple, grinning expression that suits lighthearted teasing, and many people use it as a softer alternative to the laughing faces when something is silly rather than hilarious.

English idioms supply more uses. “Monkey business” is minor misbehavior, “monkeying around” is wasting time, “monkey see, monkey do” mocks imitation, and “cheeky monkey” is an affectionate British scolding. The emoji can illustrate any of them. It is also a zodiac sign, so it appears in Lunar New Year greetings during the Year of the Monkey and in birthday messages for people born in one.

The emoji has a darker record that every user should know. Comparing Black people to monkeys is an old and vicious racist insult, and 🐵 and 🐒 have been posted in large numbers under the social media accounts of Black athletes and public figures as abuse. Football authorities and social networks have publicly condemned and acted against that practice. Because of this history, sending a monkey emoji about or to a Black person can cause serious offense even when no insult is intended.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Within families and close friendships it is a pet name and a mood. “Come get your monkey from the top of the bookshelf” is a parent talking about a child. “I’m such a 🐵 today” means the sender is being goofy. It also follows small confessions of naughtiness, similar to a cheeky grin.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: This is where caution matters most. In replies to strangers, particularly Black people, monkey emojis are widely read as racist regardless of intent, and they can lead to reports, bans or public backlash. Used on your own posts about animals, travel or your kids, the emoji is unremarkable. Audience and target make all the difference.

contexts.label: In sports
contexts.body: Football in particular has had repeated incidents of players receiving monkey emojis after matches, and clubs and governing bodies have treated them as racist abuse. Even jokes between teammates that leaned on monkey imagery have ended in disciplinary action. Fans and athletes are best advised to leave it out of sports talk entirely.

combos.meaning: Bananas, snack time, or going “bananas” with excitement.
See no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil; the three wise monkeys, a different set from 🐵.
Jungle, tropical travel or a zoo visit.

confusedWith.difference: 🙈 covers its eyes and is used for embarrassment, shyness or “I can’t look.” It is one of the most popular emojis and reads as an emotion. 🐵 has its hands down and simply represents a monkey or monkey-like silliness.
🐒 is a full-body monkey sitting or walking with a long tail. It is used more literally for the animal. Both versions share the playful meaning and the same potential to be read as a racist slur.
🦍 is a large dark ape used for strength, gym talk and brute force. It carries the same risk as other primate emojis when aimed at people, but in neutral use it suggests power rather than mischief.

avoid: Never use it in reference to a Black person or in replies to their posts; it is widely understood as racist abuse.
Avoid it in sports commentary and fan arguments, where monkey emojis have a documented history of abuse.
Do not call an adult colleague a monkey with it, since the comparison is demeaning in professional settings.
design: The glyph is a monkey’s face seen from the front: brown fur, a lighter tan face and large round ears. Apple, Google and Samsung give it a neutral or gently smiling mouth. It is the base design for the three wise monkey emojis, which add hands over the eyes, ears or mouth. Platform versions differ in shading and outline only.

faqs.a: The emoji itself is not, but it is used as racist abuse when aimed at Black people, echoing a long-standing dehumanizing insult. Social platforms and sports organizations recognize this. Used about animals, children you know or yourself, it is harmless.

faqs.q: What does 🐵 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: Normally that they are being silly or calling you cheeky in a fond way. It is a playful, childlike emoji, not a flirtatious one. If it arrives from a stranger in a hostile exchange, treat it as an insult.
🙈 is the see-no-evil monkey hiding its eyes, and people use it for shyness or cringing. 🐵 is the plain monkey face. If you want to say “I’m embarrassed,” choose 🙈; for goofing around, 🐵 fits.

faqs.q: When did the monkey face emoji come out?
faqs.a: It has been in the standard emoji set since 2010, alongside the full-body monkey and the three wise monkeys. Later releases added the gorilla and orangutan for people who want a different primate.
